---
title: "Retaining data in fitted models"
description: "Choose store_data and lean without losing the operations your analysis needs."
sidebar: reference
---

`store_data=False` discards the retained estimation data and model frames.
`lean=True` additionally discards large estimation arrays, residuals, fitted
values, and solver state. The result keeps coefficients, inference, model and
sample descriptions, and its estimation options. Removed attributes are
absent rather than set to `None`.

The table below demonstrates ordinary unweighted OLS **without absorbed fixed
effects**. Other estimators, designs, and inference modes can need more state.

```{python}
#| results: asis
import pandas as pd
import pyfixest as pf
from pyfixest.errors import MissingModelDataError

data = pf.get_data(N=100, seed=1234)
storage_modes = {
    "Default": {},
    "store_data=False": {"store_data": False},
    "lean=True": {"lean": True},
}
rows = []
for name, options in storage_modes.items():
    fit = pf.feols("Y ~ X1 + X2", data, **options)
    operations = {
        "Coefficients": lambda: fit.coef(),
        "Coefficient table": lambda: fit.tidy(),
        "Residuals": lambda: fit.resid(),
        "In-sample predictions": lambda: fit.predict(),
        "Predictions on supplied new data": lambda: fit.predict(newdata=data.head()),
    }
    row = {"Storage": name}
    for operation, call in operations.items():
        try:
            call()
            row[operation] = "Available"
        except MissingModelDataError:
            row[operation] = "Requires retained state"
    rows.append(row)
print(pd.DataFrame(rows).set_index("Storage").T.to_markdown())
```

## Plan the operations you need

- Compute residual-based statistics before discarding residuals.
- Supply `newdata=` when predicting from a lean linear fit. Those predictions
  use its retained formula specification and coefficients.
- Fixed-effect prediction needs recovered effects. A stripped fit cannot
  recover them from discarded original data; supported workflows must retain
  or recover the required state.
- Covariance updates and resampling can require designs, scores, original
  data, or refits. Choose inference at estimation time when retaining less data.
- IV first-stage models follow the same storage policy as their parent fit.

## Know when state appears

`fit.options`, `fit.model`, `fit.sample_info`, `fit.fitstat`,
and `fit.capabilities` describe completed fits. Some components require a
specific estimator or operation:

| Component | Availability |
| --- | --- |
| `fit.coeftable`, `fit.variance_covariance` | Fits with estimated coefficients and inference; absent on fixed-effects-only OLS fits |
| `fit.first_stage` | IV fits |
| `fit.fixef_estimates` | After successful `fit.fixef()` |
| `fit.ritest_statistics` | After `fit.ritest(..., store_ritest_statistics=True)` |
| `fit.wald` | After a supported Wald test; an initial test is computed for eligible non-IV OLS fits |
| `fit.solution` | Quantile solver state where published; removed by `lean=True` |

When required state is absent, `MissingModelDataError` names the operation
and gives the refitting remedy. Model support and retained state are separate:
retaining data cannot enable an operation the estimator does not support.

See [model support](/reference-guide/model-support.qmd),
[`EstimationOptions`](/reference/estimation.state.EstimationOptions.qmd), and
[`fit.predict()`](/reference/estimation.models.feols_.Feols.predict.qmd).
